idiom_name: struct with an immutable ID field and an explicit Equal method (or pointer identity)
implementation_notes: Go has no equality overloading, so the classic structure is replaced by convention: the entity is a struct whose first field is an immutable ID (a named type such as type CustomerID string or a uuid.UUID), state changes go through methods on *Customer, and comparisons use a.ID == b.ID or an explicit Equal method rather than == on the struct - Go compares struct values field by field, so struct equality would include every mutable attribute. Identity travels with the value; when a single in-memory instance must be shared, hold *Customer and rely on pointer comparison, which the specification defines as equality of the pointed-to variable. Persistence sits behind a repository interface that resolves ids to *Customer and recreates the value from rows, keeping the struct free of database tags.
pitfalls: c1 == c2 on the struct compares every field including mutable state, so two copies of the same customer compare unequal after one is renamed; always compare ID.
Copying an entity struct (assignment, function argument, map value) duplicates the identity and the two copies then diverge; pass *Customer for entities and reserve value semantics for value objects.
Using the database's auto-increment key as ID couples the model to storage and makes the identity unknown before insert; a store-independent id type lets new entities have identity immediately.
